faq.q: What is white light made of?
faq.a: White light, like sunlight, is a mixture of all the colours of the rainbow: red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet. A prism or a raindrop can split it into those colours.
asks: What colours are in white light?

faq.q: What happens to the colours an object absorbs?
faq.a: The absorbed colours are not seen. Their energy is turned into a little heat, which is why dark things warm up in the sun.
asks: Where does the absorbed light go?
Why do dark clothes get hot?

faq.q: Why are white things white and black things black?
faq.a: A white object reflects almost all colours of light, and all of them mixed look white. A black object absorbs almost all colours, so very little light comes back to your eye.
asks: Why does white paper look white?

faq.q: Why does a red apple look black under blue light?
faq.a: A red apple can only reflect red light. Blue light has no red in it, so the apple absorbs it and reflects almost nothing, and it looks dark or black.
asks: What colour is a red thing in blue light?
Why do colours change under coloured lights?

faq.q: Does an apple have a colour in the dark?
faq.a: In total darkness there is no light to reflect, so nothing reaches your eyes and you see no colour at all. Colour needs light.
asks: What colour are things in the dark?
Is colour still there when the lights are off?

facts: Isaac Newton showed in the 1660s that a prism splits white sunlight into a spectrum of colours.
Human eyes have three kinds of colour-sensing cone cells, most sensitive to long (red), medium (green) and short (blue) wavelengths.
Black objects absorb most visible light, so they warm up faster in sunshine than white ones.

quiz.say: A green leaf is lit only by red light. What colour does it look?
quiz.show: A green leaf under pure red light looks…
quiz.why: The leaf reflects mainly green light. Red light has no green in it, so the leaf absorbs most of it and looks dark.

wrong.0: It can only look green if green light is shining on it.
wrong.2: A green leaf absorbs most red light rather than reflecting it.
